full_judgment:
2. Plaintiff is the petitioner before this Court It was his short case that the suit land was leased out to the plaintiff and one Azahar Bahadur by the owners of the property in 1351 BS on receiving salami and also at a rental of Taka 2.25 by issuing Amaldari and Dakhilas and delivered possession to the plaintiff and others. Since 1351 BS the plaintiff was in peaceful possession of Ka schedule land by residing in the homestead portion, planting trees in the garden portion and cultivating the same land of the schedule on paying rent to the landlord continuously and without any interruption from any quarter. Though the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land in the year 1351 BS in the SA record his name was not recorded and for correction of record of right the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 258 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif, Barisal and obtained a compromise decree on 14.5.76. Thereafter the plaintiff filed an application under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which was registered as Mutation Case No. 193G/75-76 in the Office of the Circle Officer (Rev) Gournadi and accordingly, a separate khatian was opened with regard to Ka schedule land. Since then he has been paying rent to the Government. The land is not enlisted as Vested and Non-resident property. It is alleged that on the basis of a false report from the Tahsildar, the Sub-Divisional Officer, Sadar, (North) Barisal started the impugned VP Case No. 142 of 1980 and was also threatening to lease out the suit property to others by dispossessing the plaintiff from there. The plaintiff had no knowledge about the aforesaid VP Case and he came to learn it on 21.1.81 and that is why the plaintiff instituted the suit for declaration that the VP Case No. 142 of 1980 is illegal, collusive, fraudulent and without jurisdiction and also for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from leasing out the suit property to anybody else. 

 7. Let me consider the suit on merit. The lower Appellate Court found that the plaintiff failed to produce any document to show that whether the plaintiff took lease of it in the year 1351 BS. Mr. Quayum submits that Ext. 3 and Ext. 4 solen am a were filed in Title Suit No. 256 of 1976. He submits that for some reason the plaintiff could not produce lease document and dakhilas of the year 1351 BS but the fact remains that since his name was not recorded in the SA record he filed the suit for correction vide Title Suit No. 258 of 1976 which was decreed on compromise on 14.5.76. Thereafter he started a Mutation Case under section 54 of the SAT Act and separate khatian was opened in his name in respect of Ka schedule land. Since then he has been paying rent to the Government. Mr. Quayum submits that had the suit property been, enlisted as enemy property, his name would not have been recorded in the SA record of right in the aforesaid Mutation Case and his rents could not be accepted by the Government. Mr. Quayum submits that in the year 1976 the aforesaid Title Suit was instituted but the suit property was enlisted as enemy property in 1980. I find substance in the contention of Mr. Quayum. Mr. Quayum submits that on 14.5.76 compromise decree was passed in Title Suit No. 258 of 1976 and in pursuance of the aforesaid decree plaintiff mutated his name in the SA record of right and had been paying rent to the Government regularly. Rightly or wrongly a decree was passed in the year 1976 when the property was not shown listed as enemy property. The aforesaid compromise decree still stands valid. Unless and until a decree of a court is set aside by a competent court it will remain as a valid decree.
